u0: No client is currently waiting and nothing has just happened, so the shop is idle and all obligations are clear. Keep watch for a client arriving; once one does, its order, pantry pickup, stove preparation and serving all become owed. If food slips on a step here, it must be retrieved on the very next step.
u1: A slip just occurred on the previous step, so a food portion is on the ground and the immediate retry is underway: the next pickup must recover the food at this very step. Only after the food is back in hand does anything else resume, and any answer for a client still owed remains outstanding. If the food is not picked up now, or a new client arrives while the hands stay empty, the task fails for good.
u10: A client has just arrived while carrying food already prepared at the stove. The order must be taken next, and then the prepared food handed over at the counter. If the food slips before the serve, it must be recovered on the very next step.
u11: A client is waiting with the order taken and food already prepared in hand. The only remaining step is to serve them at the counter. Any slip of the carried food must be undone on the immediately following step.
u12: A client's order was just served while carrying food that had been prepared, and no client is waiting. The arrival is complete; prepare for the next client, whose order, preparation and serving will all be owed. The carried prepared portion stays relevant only to a future client.
u13: A client's order was just served, no client remains, and the hands are empty. No obligations are outstanding until the next arrival comes. Be ready to take a new order as soon as someone arrives.
u14: A client is waiting whose order is taken and whose food was just prepared at the stove, yet nothing is carried because the food slipped on that very step. The food on the ground must be picked up on the very next step, and then served to the waiting client. Failing the immediate pickup fails the task.
u15: A client is waiting with the order taken, food in hand ready, and the prepared food already served. The arrival is complete; the shop returns to idle until the next client appears. The carried portion can be held for the next client's needs.
u16: A client has just arrived while food that was prepared is still being carried. Take the order at the counter next, then hand the prepared food over. Any slip requires recovery on the following step.
u17: A slip occurred on the previous step during processing of a newly arrived client whose order has not yet been taken, and the food is on the ground with empty hands. The very next step must pick up the food to avoid failing. After that, the order, a possible re-prepare, and serving all remain owed. Prepare can only be done while carrying and with an order taken.
u18: A slip occurred just after a client's order was taken, and the food lies on the ground with empty hands. Retrieving it on the very next step is mandatory, and only then can preparation and serving follow. Any lapse at this point fails the task outright.
u19: A client's order was just handed over, but the food had slipped on that same step, so a portion is on the ground and the hands are empty. The immediate next step must pick that portion back up. This retrieval is owed regardless of the absence of a waiting client.
u2: A client has just arrived and nothing has been done for them yet. The order must be taken, food fetched from the pantry, prepared at the stove, and finally handed over, all before the task can rest. Starting with the order at the counter is the natural next step.
u20: A client has just arrived and the food was lost that same step, so the hands are empty while the client waits. The order still needs to be taken, fresh food fetched from the pantry, prepared at the stove, and served; the dropped portion must also be recovered immediately since the wait began with empty hands.
u21: The food slipped out while a client whose order is already taken waits, leaving the hands empty. The food must be picked up on the very next move to keep the promise, and the raw portion still needs to reach the stove and then the client.
u22: A client with an order taken is waiting and the food slipped away while being carried, so nothing is in hand. Picking the dropped portion up on the very next move is required, after which it must be prepared at the stove and delivered.
u23: A client whose order was already served is still recorded as waiting, and food was lost this step leaving the hands empty. The dropped portion must be retrieved on the very next move, and it then needs to be prepared and handed to the client.
u24: A client has just arrived and the food slipped away that same step, so the hands are empty. The order still has to be taken, food fetched and prepared, served, and the dropped portion recovered on the very next move.
u25: The food fell while being carried and a client whose order is taken is waiting. The next move must pick the food up, after which it still has to be prepared at the stove and served to the client.
u26: A client's order is already taken and the food slipped from the hands. The immediate pickup is mandatory, and the raw portion must then be prepared and delivered to the waiting client.
u27: The food was lost while carrying but the order had already been served, leaving the hands empty. The dropped portion must be recovered on the very next move, then prepared and served to the waiting client.
u28: A client arrived and the food slipped away on that step while the hands were empty. The order must be taken, food fetched and prepared, served, and the dropped food picked up on the very next move.
u29: The food fell while a client with a taken order waits. The food must be picked up on the next move, and after that it still needs preparing at the stove and handing to the client.
u3: A client is waiting with the order already taken, and no food is in hand. Food still has to be fetched from the pantry, prepared at the stove, and served to this client. Nothing is prepared yet, and cooking requires carrying raw food.
u30: The food slipped out of the hands and the client's order has already been taken. Recovering the portion on the very next move is required; afterwards it still has to be cooked and served.
u31: The food was dropped but the order was already served, and the hands are now empty. The very next move must retrieve the food, and the raw portion then needs preparing and handing over to the waiting client.
u32: A mandatory requirement has been violated: food that fell was not picked up on the very next move, so the task can no longer be completed successfully.
u4: A client's order was just handed over in prepared form, and now no client is waiting. The arrival is fully handled, so watch for the next client and handle it the same way. No food is carried, so the next arrival will need a fresh pantry pickup.
u5: A client is waiting whose order was taken, and their food was just prepared at the stove and served. No client remains, so the shop is idle until the next arrival. Nothing is carried now, so the next arrival restarts the cycle from the order.
u6: A client has just arrived while carrying food that has not yet been prepared. The order must be taken, the carried food prepared at the stove with the order in hand, and then served. Seek the client first, then the stove.
u7: A client is waiting with the order taken, and food is being carried raw. All that remains is to prepare it at the stove and hand it over at the counter. If the food slips en route, the very next step must retrieve it.
u8: A client's order was just served while food was still being carried, and no client is waiting now. The served client is done, and watch for the next arrival, which will need its own order, pickup, preparation and serving. The carried portion can be kept or dropped as convenient until then.
u9: A client's order was just served, no client is waiting, and no food remains in hand. The shop is idle until the next client arrives, then the full order-to-serve cycle restarts. Keep an eye out for arrivals.
